note: Samantha-bar-shaped scenarios for the memory-authority class (turns = (user, session label, text) exactly as scripts/perf/samantha_bar.py SCENARIOS; asks = (user, question)). They are NOT wired into the live bar (that is a baseline decision: new scenario ids need a --record-baseline run on a healthy box) - tests/test_memory_authority.py replays each one at the STORE level: seed rows, then the model-proposed facts are ingested with the day's user turns as the anchor. Synthetic people/places only.

scenarios.title: an inference cannot overwrite what I said
scenarios.proves: a day transcript with a half-heard sentence about someone else does not turn the stated dog name into the heard one; the heard one waits as a candidate
turns: uh Rex is coming over I think, we will see about the shopping

scenarios.title: a name I only overheard is a person, not me
scenarios.proves: a speech-to-text fragment naming a third person never becomes the owner's name; the name is raised as a person to ask about
turns: Okay, that is the plan for tomorrow and the shopping.
uh Mika Vale is coming over I think, and so on

expect_pending: Mika Vale was mentioned in conversation (who they are is not known).

scenarios.title: a model's reading of 'I stopped' waits for my yes
scenarios.proves: 'I don't play tennis any more' read by the turn digest is user_stated_derived: it beats model classes but never a direct statement, so it parks as a candidate the person approves (a direct writer would have retired the old fact at once)
turns: I don't play tennis any more.

scenarios.title: a model-read move and a guess both wait; neither overwrites
scenarios.proves: after 'I live in Hobart now' the turn digest's reading is user_stated_derived and a consolidation guess is inferred: both are held as candidates against the direct 'I live in Dunedin' row
turns: I live in Dunedin, by the way.
Big news - I've moved. I live in Hobart now.
asks: Which city do I live in these days?
